conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (the EPDS). It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days, and it helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up after childbirth. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in immediate danger. There are no “right” answers—just whatever feels true for you. Ready to start?

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Honestly? It’s been hard. My husband will make a joke or something silly will happen and I know I *should* laugh, but most of the time it just feels flat—like I’m watching from behind a pane of glass. I did chuckle once when the baby let out this tiny burp that sounded like a squeaky toy, but even then the smile faded fast and I went right back to feeling heavy.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes, I guess... but it feels like work. I laughed a little at a silly meme my friend sent, yet it disappeared fast and I went right back to feeling empty.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even a shower without rushing. This week it’s mostly “what’s the point?” I did feel a tiny spark when my sister said she’d bring dinner, but it faded before she even got here. Everything just feels flat, like I’m going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… way more than I’d like to admit. Yesterday the baby spit up a ton right after I’d finally gotten him down for a nap, and the first thing I thought was, “I must’ve over-fed him—why can’t I figure this out?” I keep replaying little goofs in my head, telling myself a “good mom” would’ve known better. It’s not every second, but it pops up several times a day, even for stuff that’s clearly not my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there feeding the baby and suddenly picture him stopping breathing, or I’ll hear a siren and imagine accidents that could happen on our street. There’s no real reason, but my heart races and I can’t settle until I check on him one more time. Sometimes I can talk myself down, but the worry just circles back an hour later.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes—three or four times this week. Out of nowhere my chest gets tight, my hands shake, and I’m convinced something awful is about to happen. No real trigger; it just floods in like a wave. I end up pacing the hallway, checking the baby monitor over and over until the feeling passes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days feel like juggling with slippery hands. I’ll start one chore, the baby cries, the phone buzzes, and suddenly I’m near tears because I can’t keep up. I manage to get through, but it’s like I’m barely treading water and the smallest extra thing—spit-up on a fresh onesie, a knock at the door—makes me feel I’m drowning.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my brain won’t shut off—keeps replaying everything I think I did wrong that day or imagining horrible "what-ifs" about the baby. It takes me over an hour to fall asleep most nights, and then I wake up at 2 or 3 a.m. with my heart racing and can’t drift off again for ages.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… pretty much every day this week. It’s like a gray cloud that follows me around. I’ll be feeding the baby and just start tearing up for no clear reason, or I’ll look out the window and feel this heavy sadness settle in. It’s not every single minute, but it’s definitely there most of the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Once was when I couldn’t get the baby to settle for almost an hour and I felt totally useless; the tears just started rolling without me even realizing. Another time was late at night when I was folding laundry and suddenly felt overwhelmed by how different everything feels.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I... I did have a couple of quick flashes—like, "what if I just drove off the road"—but I never planned anything and I’m not going to act on it. They just pop in and scare me, then I push them away. I’ve got the baby, I couldn’t... I just need these thoughts to stop.

You've shared that the past week has felt overwhelmingly gray-laughter fades quickly, nothing feels enjoyable, and you're constantly second-guessing yourself as a mum while frightening thoughts of accidents or harm intrude day and night. You described tearful episodes, restless hours lying awake replaying worries, sudden surges of panic, and fleeting images of driving off the road that scare you. Yet you also told me you love your baby and want these dark thoughts to stop so you can feel like yourself again.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 25, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports only fleeting enjoyment and persistent emptiness, aligning with "Definitely not so much now"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes complete loss of anticipatory pleasure and persistent anhedonia matching "Hardly at all"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports self-blame several times daily for minor issues, matching "some of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports daily intrusive worries and physical anxiety symptoms occurring multiple times per day, matching 'Yes, very often</sym>, <sym>Patient describes multiple unexpected panic episodes with physical symptoms and intense fear, matching "Yes, quite a lot"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent overwhelm and difficulty coping, matching "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly difficulty initiating and maintaining sleep due to racing negative thoughts, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports pervasive daily sadness ('pretty much every day,' 'most of the time') with crying spells and persistent low mood—clinically aligns with 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports two clear crying episodes this week tied to feeling "useless" and "overwhelmed," matching "Yes, quite often"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes recurrent intrusive suicidal imagery ("quick flashes" of driving off the road) that she finds distressing; this aligns with "Sometimes" having self-harm thoughts.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Score 25 places you well above the 13+ threshold indicating probable major depression. Daily <sym>depressed mood</sym>, marked <sym>loss of interest</sym>, <sym>excessive guilt</sym>, multiple <sym>panic attacks</sym>, prominent insomnia, and repeated <sym>passive suicidal thoughts</sym> meet DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset. Item 10 score of 2 flags safety concern even without intent. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent same-day appointment with your <med>GP</med>, <med>obstetric provider</med>, or local <med>perinatal mental-health team</med> to review mood, safety, and treatment options
2. Ask a trusted adult to stay with you tonight and help with baby care while you seek help
3. Remove or secure potential means of self-harm (excess medications, car keys if intrusive images persist) and keep crisis numbers handy
4. Begin daily gentle outdoor walks and 5-minute breathing exercises; short, manageable tasks can gently lift mood
5. Schedule follow-up EPDS in two weeks to track progress once treatment starts
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

Patient-reported symptoms (≥1 wk unless noted):
- Depressed mood, tearfulness: daily, persistent
- Anhedonia: marked loss of interest/pleasure in usual activities
- Excessive guilt/self-blame: several times daily ("bad mom" cognitions)
- Anxiety: daily pervasive worry, 3–4 panic-like episodes/week
- Sleep disturbance: difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep related to rumination
- Feeling overwhelmed: difficulty coping with routine tasks
- Passive suicidal ideation: fleeting, no plan or intent

Observed pattern: congruent with moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with prominent anxiety; safety risk flagged due to presence of any self-harm thoughts.

Screening significance: high likelihood—meets multiple DSM-5-TR criteria for Major Depressive Episode with peripartum onset; consider standardized tool (EPDS) and same-day safety assessment.
